scope: Proposition 4.1 (Imported geometric estimates) of the manuscript “The first lattice correction to Bloch's law” (preprints/The-first-lattice-correction-to-Blochs-law-October-5-2026/first-lattice-correction-bloch-law.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 271 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4c19762cfd46fbb0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 8-9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all sufficiently large β, every allowed pin set D, every deterministic time, every anchor x, and every R0 above a fixed threshold, the following bounds hold. Put p = (5/β)10/11. 1. The probability of a nonregular time under PD is at most CR3 0p6 + Ce−cRξ 0 , (4.1) for some fixed ξ > 0. Failure of the second regularity condition alone has probability at most Ce−cRξ 0 . 8 2. At every locally regular time, every nonnegative vector on the hole graph supported above BR0 (x) satisfies ∥v∥ 2+4/3 2 ≤ CDt(v)∥v∥ 4/3 1 . (4.2) There is an available slot within bounded distance of every site in B2R0 (x). Available slots over two sites in this ball at distance b can be joined by a path of length at most C(1 + b), staying within distance C(1 + b) of the first site and inside B3R0 (x). 3. At every regular time, each available slot a above BR0 (x) admits a unit flow Ja to infinity on the extended hole graph. For b the distance between its source site and an edge, |Ja(e)| ≤ C(1 + b)−199/100 , |Ja(e)| ≤ C(1 + b)−2 (b ≤ R0). (4.3) All constants are uniform in the volume, pins, anchor, and deterministic time.
